prs.title: fix: allow integer file descriptors for errlog in stdio_client
prs.author: RudrenduPaul
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: sys.stderr (a TextIO) cannot be passed to subprocess in certain environments (e.g. Jupyter kernels), causing failures when spawning stdio server processes. members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2410: sys.stderr (a TextIO) cannot be passed to subprocess in certain environments (e.g. Jupyter kernels), causing failures when spawning stdio server processes. PR #2020 adds a Jupyter-detection heuristic and presumably substitutes a safe default internally; PR #2410 solves the same root cause more generally by widening the errlog type to TextIO | int, letting callers explicitly pass subprocess.DEVNULL or any integer FD. Once #2410 is merged, the Jupyter-specific detection in #2020 becomes unnecessary because Jupyter users can simply pass subprocess.DEVNULL.

clusters.pick_reason: The two PRs take different approaches to the same root problem. #1849 adds a RuntimeError guard at ClientSession entry, preventing use outside a context manager — this catches misuse but does not address what happens when the underlying I/O channel breaks during a live session. #2567 targets the stdio transport layer's stdout reader and handles BrokenResourceError directly, which is the proximate cause of hangs: an unhandled exception in the reader task silently kills it, leaving the session waiting forever. The approach difference outweighs the age tiebreaker favoring #1849.
